subject: ClearStream OneTrust profile: ownership & CAIQ mapping kickoff
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearstream.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: security@clearstream.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 26 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood onboarding for OneTrust — evidence owners + CAIQ slices

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the quick intro call earlier. As discussed, ClearStream is beginning a OneTrust profile refresh and we'd like Redwood's help to:

- identify which CAIQ sections you will answer vs. which we should map or proxy;
- agree on canonical filenames and evidence TTL for the profile; and
- surface a single owner for each evidence item so our portal automation can pick uploads.

Can you confirm who at Redwood will own the CAIQ mapping and whether you prefer us to accept uploads from an S3 manifest or via the OneTrust UI? Ideally we'd have an agreed manifest format by end of next week.

A few notes from our side: we need SOC 2 artifacts (in-scope controls) and the CAIQ answers scoped to data-in-rest and API boundaries. We also have a short security Q&A that will require sign-off from the engineering lead.

Proposed kickoff: Thu Apr 28 10:00 PDT (30 min) — will that work?

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Security Programs Lead
ClearStream

Attachments: none
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearstream.com>, security@clearstream.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 26 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding for OneTrust — evidence owners + CAIQ slices

Hi Maya,

Appreciate the clear direction. Yes, Thu Apr 28 10:00 PDT works for our team — I booked the slot and sent a calendar invite.

Quick answers up front:
- Owner model: Redwood will provide a draft evidence ownership matrix that assigns a primary owner (product, infra, or security) with a delegated uploader. We ask ClearStream to accept the delegated uploader (service account) in OneTrust or allow S3 manifest ingestion.
- CAIQ mapping: Aditya will lead the initial CAIQ->OneTrust field mapping and provide a CSV you can ingest. We'll include flags for "we answer" vs "vendor-provided" vs "third-party".
- Manifest format: we use an S3 manifest (JSON lines) that points to signed artifacts; we'll provide an example and the CSV mapping by Apr 30.

I've attached the first-pass evidence matrix and a mapping template to the repo — these are drafts and should help structure the kickoff.

See you Thu — agenda will be: 1) scope & in-scope controls, 2) mapping approach (CSV + manifest), 3) upload mechanism & roles, 4) timeline to populate OneTrust.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Manager, Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx, caiaq-to-onetrust-mapping_v1.csv
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearstream.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 Apr 2028 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding for OneTrust — evidence owners + CAIQ slices

On Thu, Apr 28, 2028 at 10:03 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached the first-pass evidence matrix and a mapping template to the repo — these are drafts and should help structure the kickoff.

Thanks everyone for the quick sync this morning. A few action items I captured (sending for clarity and owners):

1) Aditya: produce CAIQ->OneTrust CSV with the following columns: CAIQ_ID, CAIQ_Question, OneTrust_Field, answer_source (redwood/clearstream/third_party), evidence_required (yes/no), canonical_filename, ttl_days. Deliverable by 2028-04-30 EOD.

2) Lauren: confirm the delegated uploader account name we should whitelist (we use redwood-onetrust-uploader@redwood-svc).

3) Maya / ClearStream: confirm whether you prefer S3 manifest ingestion or manual upload via OneTrust UI. If S3, please provide a signed upload bucket name and the IAM role ARN that can write manifests.

4) Both teams: decide on TTL policy. Our recommendation: short-lived logs (60 days), config docs (365 days), SOC artifacts (3 years) unless compliance requires longer. We will tag each artifact in the manifest with ttl_days.

Quick question — for control evidence that references cloud logs, do you want us to point to a redacted sample plus a link to process documentation, or should we provide full ingestion artifacts? We generally push samples + runbooks to minimize exposure.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearstream.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2028 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding for OneTrust — evidence owners + CAIQ slices

On Thu, Apr 28, 2028 at 10:35 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> 3) Maya / ClearStream: confirm whether you prefer S3 manifest ingestion or manual upload via OneTrust UI. If S3, please provide a signed upload bucket name and the IAM role ARN that can write manifests.

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the suggested TTL defaults, they look reasonable. ClearStream prefers S3 manifest ingestion for bulk imports. We will:

- Create a short-lived upload bucket and share the ARN and a pre-signed manifest example by Wed May 1 EOD.
- Accept the redwood-onetrust-uploader@redwood-svc service account if you can provide a canonical email for the uploader (we'll add to our allowlist).
- For log-based evidence we prefer redacted samples + a runbook link. Please mark any PII in artifacts with [REDACTED] and call out redaction in the manifest metadata.

We'll review Aditya's CSV mapping once it's posted to the Drive link you shared. Sending the bucket ARN and a OneTrust ingestion test URL shortly.

Best,
Maya Patel
Security Programs Lead
ClearStream

Attachments: none
